original_question: For a compact Riemann surface X of genus g >= 2 and the moduli space SU_X(r) of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, let L denote the determinant line bundle on SU_X(r). The base locus of the linear system |L| consists of those bundles E such that h^0(X, E ⊗ M) ≠ 0 for every line bundle M of degree g-1 on X. Beyond the examples constructed by Raynaud, for which other ranks r do such base points occur, can this base locus have positive dimension, and can one obtain a reasonable upper bound for its dimension?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Question 1 (the open problem on the base locus of |L| on SU_X(r))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object and nearly the exact question from the paper: X is a compact Riemann surface, SU_X(r) is the moduli space of semistable rank-r bundles with trivial determinant, L is the determinant line bundle, the base-point criterion is correctly stated as h^0(X,E⊗M) != 0 for every degree-(g-1) line bundle M, and the three subquestions are exactly Beauville's: more examples for other ranks, possible positive-dimensional base locus, and an upper bound for its dimension.
missing_details: The paper quantifies over all N in J^{g-1}(X), the Picard variety of line bundles of degree g-1 on X; this parameter space should be named explicitly.
The determinant line bundle is defined by L := O(Theta_N), where Theta_N = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X,E⊗N) >= 1}, and one should state that this definition is independent of the choice of N.

The equivalence between being a base point of |L| and satisfying h^0(X,E⊗N) != 0 for every N of degree g-1 is justified by Theorem 2: the divisors Theta_N span |L|. The paper also packages this as theta(E) = J^{g-1}(X).
The paper works implicitly under the standing assumption g >= 2, after noting that the cases g <= 1 are elementary.

To make 'other values of r' fully paper-faithful, it helps to record the immediately preceding known cases: |L| is base-point free for r=2; it is base-point free for r=3 when g=2 or when g >= 3 and X is generic in the moduli of genus-g curves; and it has base points for r = ng whenever an integer n >= 2 divides g.
Because the paper uses the letter L both for the determinant line bundle on SU_X(r) and for a degree-(g-1) line bundle on X, a stand-alone reformulation should rename the latter to avoid ambiguity.
The ambient field is implicitly complex-analytic/algebraic, since X is a compact Riemann surface.
refined_question: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g >= 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and for any N in J^{g-1}(X) define Theta_N = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X,E⊗N) >= 1}; write L := O(Theta_N), which is independent of N. Then the base locus of the complete linear system |L| is B = {E in SU_X(r) | h^0(X,E⊗N) != 0 for every N in J^{g-1}(X)}. Raynaud's results show that |L| is base-point free for r=2, and for r=3 when g=2 or when g >= 3 and X is generic, while |L| has base points for r = ng whenever an integer n >= 2 divides g. Apart from these known cases, for which other ranks r can B be nonempty, can B have positive dimension, and is there a reasonable upper bound for dim B?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for which ranks r can one have theta(E) = J^{g-1}(X) for some E in SU_X(r), where theta(E) := {N in J^{g-1}(X) | h^0(X,E⊗N) >= 1}, and how large can the locus {E in SU_X(r) | theta(E) = J^{g-1}(X)} be?
justification: The draft is targeting Beauville's Question 1 in Section 3 almost verbatim. In Section 2 he defines the determinant bundle L = O(Theta_N) and proves, via Theorem 2, that the divisors Theta_N span |L|; Section 3 then identifies the base points of |L| with the bundles E such that theta(E) = J^{g-1}(X), equivalently h^0(X,E⊗N) != 0 for every degree-(g-1) line bundle N. Immediately after recalling Raynaud's known cases in Theorem 3, Beauville asks exactly whether one can find more examples for other ranks, whether the base locus can have positive dimension, and whether one can bound its dimension. So the paper-faithful target is this narrow base-locus question, not the later questions about |L^k| or etale coverings.
